category: AC/DC Module: Magnetic Field Interfaces, Magnetization Models, Coils and Magnetic Boundary Conditions
description: Magnetic interfaces of the AC/DC Module not covered elsewhere (Magnetic Field Formulation, Magnetic Fields, No Currents, Boundary Elements, Magnetic Machinery, Rotating, Time Periodic) and the domain, boundary, edge, point and pair features of the Magnetic Fields (mf), Magnetic Fields, No Currents (mfnc), Magnetic Fields, Currents Only (mfco) and Magnetic and Electric Fields (mef) interfaces, from the COMSOL 6.4 AC/DC Module User's Guide. Java type strings were verified against the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: Magnetic Field Formulation (mfh)
tools.description: Solves Maxwell's equations with the magnetic field H as the dependent variable (H-formulation, curl elements) and is especially suited to time-domain modeling of materials with strongly nonlinear E-J characteristics such as high-temperature superconductors. It supports Stationary, Frequency Domain, Small-Signal Analysis, Time Dependent and Time-to-Frequency Losses studies in 3D, 2D and 2D axisymmetry, and requires a nonzero conductivity everywhere (nonconducting air must be given a small artificial conductivity). Default nodes: Faraday's Law, Magnetic Insulation, Initial Values and Magnetic Gauss' Law.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > AC/DC > Electromagnetic Fields > Vector Formulations > Magnetic Field Formulation. Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("mfh", "MagneticFieldFormulation", "geom1")

parameters.name: Components (2D)
parameters.description: In-plane magnetic field (default; out-of-plane currents), Out-of-plane magnetic field, or Three-component.

parameters.name: Faraday's Law node
parameters.description: B-H and E-J constitutive relations (e.g. E-J power law for superconductors).

parameters.name: Magnetic Gauss' Law
parameters.description: Auxiliary potential enforcing div B = 0 (default in 2D in-plane / 3D).

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: Curl element order for H.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Superconducting/superconducting_wire: HTS tape with E-J power law in Faraday's Law, Tangential Magnetic Field excitation, Time Dependent study to compute AC loss.
tools.notes: Couple to Magnetic Fields, No Currents in the outer air with the 'Magnetic Fields Formulation Magnetic Fields No Currents Coupling' to avoid the artificial air conductivity. MHD coupling also supports mfh.

tools.name: Magnetic Fields, No Currents, Boundary Elements (mfncbe)
tools.description: Boundary element (BEM) version of the scalar-potential magnetostatics interface for current-free sources such as permanent magnets; only boundaries are meshed and the surrounding space (including infinite voids) is handled analytically. It is stationary only (3D and 2D) and can also serve as the open outer region of a Magnetic Fields or Magnetic Fields, Currents Only model instead of infinite elements. Default nodes: Magnetic Flux Conservation, Magnetic Insulation (exterior) and Initial Values.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > AC/DC > Magnetic Fields, No Currents > Magnetic Fields, No Currents, Boundary Elements. Java: physics().create("mfncbe", "MagneticFieldsNoCurrentsBoundaryElements", "geom1")

parameters.name: Domain selection
parameters.description: Manual, All domains, All voids, or All domains and voids (default); the infinite void has entity number 0.

parameters.name: Features
parameters.description: Magnetic Flux Conservation, Zero/Magnetic Scalar Potential, Normal Magnetic Flux Density, Force Calculation.

parameters.name: Couplings
parameters.description: Magnetic Scalar–Scalar Potential Coupling (with mfco) and Magnetic Vector–Scalar Potential Coupling (with mf).

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Introductory_Electromagnetic_Forces/force_calculation_02_magnetic_force_bem and force_calculation_03_magnetic_torque_bem (magnet force and torque with BEM air).
tools.notes: When combined with Magnetic Fields, the mf interface needs Gauge Fixing for A-Field and a Fully Coupled direct solver.

tools.name: Magnetic Machinery, Rotating, Time Periodic (mmtp)
tools.description: 2D interface for steady-state (periodic) operation of rotating electric machines: the out-of-plane vector potential is solved simultaneously at nTP time frames of one electrical period (Time Periodic equation form), so a full cycle including rotor motion, induced currents and losses is obtained in one stationary-type solve instead of a long transient. Stationary, Frequency Domain and Time Dependent studies are allowed for coupling. The geometry must be an assembly with rotor and stator composites, Rotating Domain and Rotational Magnetic Continuity features.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > AC/DC > Electromagnetics and Mechanics > Magnetic Machinery, Rotating, Time Periodic. Java: physics().create("mmtp", "MagneticMachineryTimePeriodic", "geom1")

parameters.name: Time periodic electrical frequency f_TP
parameters.description: User defined (default 50 Hz), From equation form (freq) or Scaled frequency.

parameters.name: Number of time frames n_TP
parameters.description: Even integer >= 2 discretizing the phase interval [0, 2*pi].

parameters.name: Motion settings
parameters.description: Rotational motion, number of poles; button Add Rotational Boundary Features.

parameters.name: Out-of-plane thickness d
parameters.description: Default 1 m; scales torque, force and voltage.

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Devices,_Motors_and_Generators/pmm_steady_state, pm_motor_2d_efficiency_map and pm_motor_2d_campbell_diagram (efficiency maps and NVH from time-periodic solutions).
tools.notes: Phase-dependent results use the suffixes _tpph and _tpN (e.g. mmtp.normB_tp0). Multiphase Winding has built-in losses here.

tools.name: Ampère's Law in Solids / Fluids (Magnetic Fields)
tools.description: Domain node of Magnetic Fields that adds Ampère's law with the material's B-H and Jc-E constitutive relations. Ampère's Law in Solids evaluates properties in the material frame and offers every magnetization model (Relative permeability, B-H curve, Magnetic losses, Remanent flux density, Magnetization, Effective B-H curve, Jiles–Atherton hysteresis, Nonlinear permanent magnet, Analytic magnetization curve, External material); Ampère's Law in Fluids (spatial frame) offers only Relative permeability and Magnetization. It replaced the 6.1-and-earlier Material type Solid/Nonsolid switch.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields > Domains > Ampère's Law in Solids / Ampère's Law in Fluids. Java: physics("mf").create("als1", "AmperesLawSolid", 3); feature("als1").set("ConstitutiveRelationBH", "BHCurve"); (fluids: "AmperesLawFluid")

parameters.name: ConstitutiveRelationBH
parameters.description: RelativePermeability, BHCurve, MagneticLosses, RemanentFluxDensity, Magnetization, EffectivePermeabilityHL (effective B-H), JilesAtherton, nonlinear PM, analytic curve, external material.

parameters.name: ConstitutiveRelationJcE
parameters.description: ElectricalConductivity, LinearizedResistivity, effective medium, etc.

parameters.name: Electric field (D-E)
parameters.description: Relative permittivity for displacement currents.

parameters.name: Loss Calculation subnode
parameters.description: Steinmetz/Bertotti iron losses.

tools.notes: The existing entry 'Ampere's Law' gives the general node; this entry documents the 6.4 Solids/Fluids split and magnetization-model list. Magnetohydrodynamics requires the Fluids variant in the fluid.

tools.name: B-H Curve / Effective B-H Curve (magnetization models)
tools.description: Nonlinear soft-magnetic constitutive relations of Ampère's Law, Magnetic Flux Conservation, Laminated Core and Passive Conductor. B-H curve uses |H| = f(|B|) (plus magnetic coenergy density) from the material's interpolation function, for stationary and transient studies. Effective B-H curve is a frequency-domain approximation that replaces the saturating material with a field-amplitude-dependent linear permeability chosen so that cycle-averaged energy (or another criterion) matches the nonlinear case, avoiding a full transient.
tools.usage: Ampère's Law in Solids > Constitutive Relation B-H > Magnetization model: B-H curve / Effective B-H curve (material properties group 'B-H curve' / 'Effective B-H curve')

parameters.name: normH / normHeff
parameters.description: Magnetic field norm function of |B| (From material or user defined).

parameters.name: Wpm / coenergy
parameters.description: Magnetic coenergy density used for energy-based lamination and forces.

parameters.name: Effective B-H criterion
parameters.description: Generated with the Effective Nonlinear Magnetic Curves Calculator (e.g. Average energy method).

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Applications/effective_nonlinear_magnetic_curves (generate effective curves from a B-H curve) and ACDC_Module/Applications/bh_curve_checker (check/extrapolate measured B-H data before use).
tools.notes: The AC/DC material library contains many soft irons and steels with B-H curves. Effective B-H curves ignore higher harmonics; use Time Dependent + Time-to-Frequency Losses for accurate iron losses.

tools.name: Hysteresis Jiles–Atherton Model (magnetization model)
tools.description: Vectorial, optionally anisotropic Jiles–Atherton hysteresis model for ferromagnetic materials with B = mu0*(H + M), where M evolves from a Langevin anhysteretic curve with five parameters: saturation magnetization Ms, domain wall density a, pinning loss k (kp), magnetization reversibility c (cr) and interdomain coupling alpha (tensors allowed). It yields hysteresis loops and hysteresis losses in time-dependent or quasi-static parametric analyses.
tools.usage: Ampère's Law in Solids (or Magnetic Flux Conservation in Solids) > Magnetization model: Hysteresis Jiles–Atherton model. Parameters MsJA, aJA, kJA, cJA, alphaJA

parameters.name: MsJA
parameters.description: Saturation magnetization (default 1e6 A/m).

parameters.name: aJA, kJA
parameters.description: Domain wall density and pinning loss (default 200 A/m, 300 A/m).

parameters.name: cJA, alphaJA
parameters.description: Reversibility (0.7) and interdomain coupling.

parameters.name: inStationaryStudy
parameters.description: TransientInitialization (default) or Parametric hysteresis for stationary sweeps over time instants.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Verifications/vector_hysteresis_modeling (anisotropic vector hysteresis); the AC/DC material library has a 'Jiles–Atherton Hysteretic Material' example.
tools.notes: Discretization section controls the order of the J-A variables. Not usable in Frequency Domain studies.

tools.name: Remanent Flux Density / Nonlinear Permanent Magnet / Magnetization (permanent-magnet models)
tools.description: Constitutive relations for permanent magnets: Remanent flux density uses B = mu0*mu_rec*H + Br with recoil permeability mu_rec and |Br| from the material times a direction field (valid in the linear recoil region); Magnetization uses B = mu0*(H + M) with a prescribed M; Nonlinear permanent magnet uses a B-H relation shifted by the coercive field Hc to capture self-demagnetization of soft magnets such as AlNiCo (example material 'Nonlinear Permanent Magnet', AlNiCo 5 approximation).
tools.usage: Ampère's Law in Solids / Magnetic Flux Conservation / Magnet > Constitutive Relation B-H > Remanent flux density | Magnetization | Nonlinear permanent magnet

parameters.name: mur_rec, normBr
parameters.description: Recoil permeability and remanent flux density norm (From material; AC/DC library has NdFeB, SmCo, ferrite grades).

parameters.name: e (direction)
parameters.description: Remanent flux direction; Magnet features compute it from North/South boundaries.

parameters.name: Hc
parameters.description: Coercive field for the nonlinear PM model.

tools.example: Magnet node in ACDC_Module/Devices,_Motors_and_Generators/linear_motor_2d uses Remanent flux density with an alternating Linear pattern of magnetization directions.
tools.notes: Do not use Nonlinear permanent magnet in Frequency Domain studies. Demagnetization with hysteresis needs the Analytic Magnetization Curve or Jiles–Atherton options.

tools.name: Magnetic Losses / Analytic Magnetization Curve / External Material (Ampère's Law B-H options)
tools.description: Further magnetization models of Ampère's Law in Solids: Magnetic losses uses a complex permeability mu_r = mu' - i*mu'' (positive mu'' for loss) in frequency-domain studies, e.g. ferrites; Analytic magnetization curve uses B = mu0(H + M(H) + Mr) with Langevin, hyperbolic tangent or linear shape functions and optional Jiles–Atherton hysteresis (magnetization components become extra DOFs); External material calls a compiled user library for |H| = f(|B|).
tools.usage: Ampère's Law in Solids > Magnetization model: Magnetic losses | Analytic magnetization curve | External material

parameters.name: murPrim, murBis
parameters.description: Real and imaginary relative permeability (Magnetic losses).

parameters.name: MagnetizationModel, Ms, chi0, Mr
parameters.description: Shape function (LangevinFunction...), saturation, initial susceptibility and remanent magnetization (Analytic curve).

parameters.name: Hysteresis
parameters.description: Enable J-A hysteresis in the analytic curve (aJAm, kJAm, cJAm, alphaJAm).

parameters.name: External material
parameters.description: Material from Global Definitions > Materials > External Material.

tools.example: Ferrite core in a frequency sweep: Ampère's Law in Solids, Magnetic losses with mu' = 2000, mu'' = 20; read core loss from mf.Qh integrated over the core.
tools.notes: Magnetic losses is not available in Magnetic Fields, Currents Only. Analytic Magnetization Curve is also used by the Nonlinear Magnetostriction coupling.

tools.name: Magnet (Magnetic Fields / Magnetic Fields, No Currents)
tools.description: Domain feature that models one or many permanent magnets and automates the magnetization direction: Specify north and south boundaries (direction from the pole-face centroids), Specify by domains (Domain Direction subnodes) or User defined vector. Circular or Linear patterns with Repeating, Alternating or User defined periodicity set directions for arrays such as rotor poles and Halbach rings. In conducting configurations it can insulate each magnet segment (to compute eddy-current losses in segmented magnets) and accepts a Loss Calculation subnode. Called Conducting Magnet / Nonconducting Magnet in Rotating Machinery, Magnetic.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields (or mfnc, mmtp) > Magnet (default subnodes North, South). Java: physics("mfnc").create("mag1", "Magnet", 3); feature("mag1").set("PatternType", "CircularPattern"); set("PeriodicType", "Alternating")

parameters.name: DirectionMethod
parameters.description: SpecifyNorthSouthBoudaries, specify by domains, or UserDefined (directionInput).

parameters.name: PatternType / PeriodicType
parameters.description: NoPattern, CircularPattern, LinearPattern; Repeating, Alternating, UserDefined (PatternAdditionalAngle).

parameters.name: PatternCenter / PatternAxis
parameters.description: Center and axis of circular patterns.

parameters.name: ConstitutiveRelationBH
parameters.description: RemanentFluxDensity (default) or other magnet models.

parameters.name: ConstrainForInducedCurrents
parameters.description: NoInducedCurrentsConstrain or WithinEachDomain (insulated segments).

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Devices,_Capacitive/hall_effect_sensor (mfnc Magnet), ACDC_Module/Devices,_Motors_and_Generators/induced_voltage_moving_magnet and tubular_permanent_magnet_generator (mf Magnet).
tools.notes: For odd counts with Alternating patterns specify the poles of the first magnet. Domain Direction subnodes override directions per domain.

tools.name: Domain Direction / North / South (Magnet subnodes)
tools.description: Subnodes that define magnetization direction for the Magnet feature: North and South select the exterior boundaries acting as the north and south pole faces (the direction goes from the south to the north pole centroid), and Domain Direction, added when the Direction method is Specify by domains, applies either north/south boundaries or a user-defined vector to a subset of the magnet domains. Several Domain Direction nodes can be stacked under one Magnet.
tools.usage: Magnet > North / South (default) or Magnet > Domain Direction (Direction method: Specify by domains). Java: feature("mag1").create("domdir1", "DomainDirection", 3); types North / South on boundaries

parameters.name: North / South selection
parameters.description: Pole-face boundaries of the magnet(s).

parameters.name: Domain Direction method
parameters.description: Specify north and south boundaries or User defined direction.

tools.example: Halbach array (ACDC_Module/Introductory_Magnetostatics/static_field_halbach_rotor_3d): one Magnet with several Domain Direction subnodes, each with a user-defined direction rotated by 90 degrees.
tools.notes: North/South must be exterior boundaries of the magnet domains.

tools.name: Laminated Core (Magnetic Fields / No Currents / Machinery)
tools.description: Domain feature for laminated soft-magnetic cores that develop no macroscopic eddy currents: magnetization model B-H curve (default), Effective B-H curve or Relative permeability, and a Lamination model Homogeneous (default), Out-of-plane (2D) or Direction based, which homogenizes a stack of steel sheets and insulation along a lamination direction with a stacking factor using energy/coenergy-based relations. An optional Loss Model gives a volumetric loss density that is user defined or from Steinmetz/Bertotti coefficients, and a Stabilization section improves robustness. Called 'Laminated Core, Ampère's Law' in Rotating Machinery, Magnetic.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields > Laminated Core. Java: physics("mf").create("lc1", "LaminatedCore", 3); set("LaminationModel", "DirectionBased"); set("StackingFactor", "98[%]")

parameters.name: LaminationModel
parameters.description: Homogeneous, OutOfPlane (2D) or DirectionBased (Direction vector).

parameters.name: StackingFactor
parameters.description: Volume fraction of steel in the stack.

parameters.name: LossModel
parameters.description: userDefined, Steinmetz (kh, alpha, beta) or Bertotti (kh, beta, sigma, lamination thickness d, kc).

parameters.name: ConstitutiveRelationBH
parameters.description: BHCurve, effective B-H curve or RelativePermeability.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Inductive/ecore_transformer: E-core as Laminated Core with Steinmetz losses, 0.35 mm sheets, B-H curve steel.
tools.notes: For solid (non-laminated) conducting iron use Ampère's Law in Solids or Passive Conductor so eddy currents are modelled.

tools.name: Passive Conductor (Magnetic Fields / Machinery)
tools.description: Domain feature for conducting metal parts that are neither magnets, laminated cores nor connected to an external circuit (copper shields, aluminium housings, rotor cages): it supports internally circulating eddy currents, optional insulation between domains like the Magnet feature, and soft-magnetic models (Relative permeability, B-H curve, Effective B-H curve). A Loss Calculation subnode gives eddy-current loss.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields / Rotating Machinery, Magnetic / Magnetic Machinery, Rotating, Time Periodic > Passive Conductor. Java: physics("rmm").create("pcond1", "PassiveConductor", 3)

parameters.name: Constitutive Relation B-H
parameters.description: Relative permeability, B-H curve or Effective B-H curve.

parameters.name: Constitutive Relation Jc-E
parameters.description: Conductivity model, identical to the Magnet node (including insulation constraints).

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Motors_and_Generators/rotating_machinery_3d_tutorial and pm_motor_2d_campbell_diagram (rotor sleeve/housing as Passive Conductor).
tools.notes: Use Coil (Single conductor) instead when the conductor is driven by a voltage/current.

tools.name: Coil (Magnetic Fields) – conductor models, litz wire and excitation
tools.description: Domain or boundary feature that turns a lumped excitation into distributed current and reports coil impedance, inductance and resistance. Conductor models: Single conductor (massive conductor with skin/proximity effects), Homogenized multiturn (N insulated thin wires as an effective medium) and Homogenized litz coil (twisted multi-strand bundles, DC resistance per length and strand count). Excitations: Current (default), Voltage, Circuit (current), Circuit (voltage) and Power (2D only); in 3D multiturn coils the Coil type is Numeric, Circular, Linear or User defined, and in 2D a Coil group connects cross-sections in series.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields > Coil (domain or boundary). Java: physics("mf").create("coil1", "Coil", 3); set("ConductorModel", "Multi"); set("CoilType", "Numeric"); set("CoilExcitation", "Current"); set("ICoil", "1[A]"); set("N", "100")

parameters.name: ConductorModel
parameters.description: Single (default), Multi (homogenized multiturn) or litz.

parameters.name: CoilExcitation
parameters.description: Current, Voltage, CircuitCurrent, CircuitVoltage, Power (2D).

parameters.name: N, wireProperties, sigmaCoil
parameters.description: Number of turns, From conductivity/resistivity/resistance/mutually coupled circuit, wire conductivity (default 6e7 S/m).

parameters.name: AreaFrom
parameters.description: FillingFactor (default 0.8), Diameter, SWG, AWG or UserDefined wire area.

parameters.name: HarmonicLoss
parameters.description: Include intrinsic AC (skin/proximity) loss of the wires in frequency domain.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Inductive/inductor_3d: 3D Coil with Circuit (current) excitation, Geometry Analysis subnode and a Coil Geometry Analysis study step, results mf.RCoil_1, mf.LCoil_1.
tools.notes: Complements the existing 'Coil (Homogenized Multiturn)' entry. Avoid step-current excitation in Time Dependent studies; the Single Conductor Coil node is obsolete in favour of Conductor model = Single conductor.

tools.name: Geometry Analysis with Input / Output (Coil subnodes)
tools.description: Subnode of a 3D Coil (Single conductor, or Homogenized multiturn with Numeric coil type) that sets up the automatic computation of the current direction field by an auxiliary current-flow problem solved in a Coil Geometry Analysis study step. Input and Output subnodes select the boundaries where current enters and leaves (none for closed loops, which need a cut), and symmetry correction factors FL and FA fix coil length and area when only part of the coil is modelled.
tools.usage: Coil > Geometry Analysis (added by default) > Input / Output. Java: feature("coil1").feature("ccc1") (type CoilCurrentCalculation); feature("ccc1").create("ct1", "CoilTerminal", 2) (Input); create("cg1", "CoilGround", 2) (Output)

parameters.name: fl (F_L)
parameters.description: Coil length multiplication factor for symmetry cuts.

parameters.name: fA (F_A)
parameters.description: Coil area multiplication factor.

parameters.name: Input / Output selections
parameters.description: Coil terminal boundaries; additional subnodes Electric Insulation, Connected Boundaries, Periodic Boundaries (for Geometry Analysis).

tools.example: Quarter model of a toroidal coil: Geometry Analysis with Input/Output on the two symmetry cuts, fl = 4, fA = 1; add Study > Coil Geometry Analysis before Frequency Domain.
tools.notes: Best results for smooth, constant cross-sections without bottlenecks. See also 'Coil Geometry Analysis' (study step, type CoilCurrentCalculation).

tools.name: Coil Geometry (Linear / Circular coil subnode)
tools.description: Subnode of a Homogenized multiturn Coil with Coil type Linear or Circular (formerly 'Reference Edge') that defines wire direction from selected edges: for Linear coils co-linear edges give the straight wire direction and length (the coil should end on exterior boundaries); for Circular coils edges forming (part of) a circle give the coil axis and azimuthal wire direction, with coil length = volume/cross-section unless the robust method is used. The 'Use robust geometry analysis method' option works without geometry (imported meshes) but needs a complete circle.
tools.usage: Coil (Coil type Circular/Linear) > Coil Geometry. Java: feature("coil1").feature("cre1") (type CoilReferenceEdge); feature("cre1").selection().set(new int[]{...})

parameters.name: Edge selection
parameters.description: Straight edges (Linear) or circular edges (Circular).

parameters.name: Use robust geometry analysis method
parameters.description: Alternative axis/direction algorithm; coil length equals the edge length.

tools.example: Solenoid around a plunger: Coil type Circular, Coil Geometry selecting the four quarter-circle edges of the winding's mid-radius circle.
tools.notes: Numeric coil type is more general for arbitrary shapes; User defined accepts any direction field.

tools.name: User Defined Coil Geometry (Coil subnode)
tools.description: Subnode of a Homogenized multiturn Coil with Coil type User defined in which the wire direction is an arbitrary vector field e_coil (analytic, or computed for example by a Curvilinear Coordinates interface) that is normalized internally, together with a coil length and optionally an overridden cross-section area. Its Input and Output subnodes mark exterior boundaries where the direction field has a normal component; they are required for Accurate voltage calculation in time/frequency studies.
tools.usage: Coil (Coil type: User defined) > User Defined Coil Geometry > Input / Output. Java: feature("coil1").feature("cg1") (type UserDefinedCoilGeometry); set("eCoil", new String[]{...}); set("length", "..."); subnodes CoilInput / CoilOutput

parameters.name: eCoil
parameters.description: Coil current flow direction vector field.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Total coil length used for resistance and voltage.

parameters.name: OverrideArea / area
parameters.description: Replace the computed cross-section area.

parameters.name: fl, fA
parameters.description: Symmetry multiplication factors.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Applications/billet_induction_heating: toroidal direction field eCoil = (0, z/sqrt(y^2+z^2), -y/sqrt(y^2+z^2)) with length (R_coil+r_coil)*pi.
tools.notes: Curvilinear Coordinates (cc) is the usual way to generate direction fields for complex shapes.

tools.name: Domain Group / Reversed Current Direction (2D coil group subnodes)
tools.description: Subnodes of a 2D or 2D-axisymmetric Coil (or Single Conductor Coil) with the Coil group option active, where all selected cross-sections are series-connected turns of one conductor. Domain Group/Boundary Group treats several domains as a single turn (parallel conductor), and Reversed Current Direction marks cross-sections where current flows antiparallel to the out-of-plane (z or azimuthal) direction, as in the return side of a winding. They can be combined freely.
tools.usage: Coil (Coil group checked) > Domain Group / Reversed Current Direction. Java: feature("coil1").create("rcd1", "ReverseCoilGroupDomain", 2) (Magnetic Fields; rmm/mmtp windings use ReversedCurrentDirection)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Cross-section domains/boundaries of the group or with reversed current.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Motors_and_Generators/linear_motor_2d: three-phase coil groups with Reversed Current Direction on the return slots.
tools.notes: Coil group assumes equal cross-section areas; for unequal areas use separate coils connected through an Electrical Circuit.

tools.name: Single Conductor Coil / Gap Feed / Boundary Feed (legacy coil features)
tools.description: Older excitation features for massive conductors: Single Conductor Coil applies a total voltage or current to a conductive domain or boundary (domain version contributes on top of Ampère's Law; in 3D it adds a coil potential V_coil and current continuity), with Gap Feed (voltage/current jump across an interior cut, for closed loops) and Boundary Feed (excitation on a terminal boundary) subnodes. It is obsolete in Magnetic Fields and Rotating Machinery, Magnetic and will be removed; use Coil with Conductor model = Single conductor.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields (legacy models) > Single Conductor Coil > Gap Feed / Boundary Feed; still used in Magnetic and Electric Fields in 2D

parameters.name: Coil excitation
parameters.description: Voltage or Current (circuit variants).

parameters.name: Coil group (2D)
parameters.description: Series connection of cross-sections.

tools.example: Open an older 5.x induction model: replace Single Conductor Coil + Gap Feed with a Coil (Single conductor) whose Geometry Analysis has Input/Output on the cut boundaries.
tools.notes: Not available in 3D for Magnetic and Electric Fields and Induction Heating; use Gap Feed with caution in frequency domain.

tools.name: Loss Calculation (Magnetic Fields subnode)
tools.description: Subnode of Ampère's Law, domain Coil, Faraday's Law, Magnetic Flux Conservation, Magnet, Passive Conductor and Multiphase Winding that computes the cycle-averaged loss density Q (W/m^3): copper loss From resistive heating (default) or, for B-H-curve, effective B-H or Jiles–Atherton materials, empirical iron-loss models Steinmetz (kh*f^alpha*B^beta) or Bertotti (hysteresis, classical eddy and excess terms with lamination thickness). In time-dependent analyses it must exist before solving and is evaluated by a subsequent Time-to-Frequency Losses study step.
tools.usage: Right-click Ampère's Law / Coil / Magnet ... > Loss Calculation. Java: feature("als1").create("loss1", "LossCalculation", 3); set("LossModel", "Steinmetz")

parameters.name: LossModel
parameters.description: fromQrh (resistive heating), Steinmetz, Bertotti, userDefined.

parameters.name: kh_steinmetz, alpha, beta_steinmetz
parameters.description: Steinmetz coefficients.

parameters.name: kh_bertotti, beta_bertotti, sigma, d, kc
parameters.description: Bertotti hysteresis/eddy/excess parameters and lamination thickness.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Inductive/ecore_transformer: Loss Calculation on the core, Time Dependent study over several periods, then a Time-to-Frequency Losses step (6 harmonics).
tools.notes: Coil losses only support 'From resistive heating'. See also 'Time-to-Frequency Losses (study step)'.

tools.name: Lumped Element (Magnetic Fields)
tools.description: Boundary feature that inserts a resistor, capacitor, inductor or general impedance between two metallic boundaries, analogous to a Lumped Port but without excitation or S-parameter output. Lumped element type: User defined impedance (default 50 ohm), Inductor (default 1 nH) or Capacitor (default 1 pF); geometry settings follow the Lumped Port (uniform, coaxial, user defined).
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields > Boundaries > Lumped Element (frequency domain, typically with Electric field/A-V formulations)

parameters.name: Lumped element name
parameters.description: Unique name used in variable names.

parameters.name: Lumped element type
parameters.description: User defined (Z_element), Inductor (L_element) or Capacitor (C_element).

parameters.name: Port geometry
parameters.description: Uniform, Coaxial or User defined, as for Lumped Port.

tools.example: Resonant RFID/wireless-power coil: Lumped Element Capacitor 680 pF across the coil gap to tune the resonance, with a Lumped Port driving the primary.
tools.notes: Java type string not present in the 6.4 Application Library. Lumped Port is catalogued separately.

tools.name: Edge Current (Magnetic Fields)
tools.description: 3D edge source that specifies a line current I0 along one or more edges (positive along the edge direction arrow), representing thin wires, overhead lines or filamentary windings without meshing their cross-section. Supports Harmonic Perturbation. Field values are singular at the edge, so evaluate at a distance.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields > Edges > Edge Current. Java: physics("mf").create("edc1", "EdgeCurrent", 1); set("Ie", "I0*exp(i*2*pi/3)")

parameters.name: Ie
parameters.description: Edge current I0 (A), default 0; complex values for phased systems.

parameters.name: harmonicPerturbation
parameters.description: Small-signal contribution flag.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Inductive/power_line_magnetic_field: three-phase line currents I0, I0*exp(i*2*pi/3), I0*exp(i*4*pi/3) on the conductor edges; also ACDC_Module/Introductory_Magnetostatics/rfid.
tools.notes: In 2D use Line Current (Out-of-Plane) at points instead.

tools.name: Line Current (Out-of-Plane) (Magnetic Fields)
tools.description: Point source in 2D and 2D-axisymmetric Magnetic Fields models that applies a current I0 flowing out of the modelling plane (z direction in 2D, azimuthal loop in 2D axisymmetry). It is the 2D counterpart of Edge Current for thin wires and filamentary loops; Line Current (on Axis) exists for axisymmetric axis points.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields > Points > Line Current (Out-of-Plane). Java: physics("mf").create("lco1", "LineCurrentOutOfPlane", 0); set("I0", "1[A]")

parameters.name: I0
parameters.description: Out-of-plane current (A).

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Verifications/thin_conductive_layer: filament current above a thin conducting sheet represented by a Transition Boundary Condition.
tools.notes: Field is singular at the point; do not evaluate forces there.

tools.name: Velocity (Lorentz Term) (Magnetic Fields)
tools.description: Domain feature that adds the motional EMF current J = sigma*(v x B) for a conductor moving with velocity v, in 2D/2D-axisymmetric Magnetic Fields (out-of-plane A only), Rotating Machinery, Magnetic and Magnetic and Electric Fields (also 3D A-V). It is valid only when the moving region is invariant along the motion (infinite or rotationally symmetric, homogeneous in the direction of motion) and contains no moving magnetic sources, e.g. a disc brake, a tube around a falling magnet or a homopolar generator.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields > Domains > Velocity (Lorentz Term). Java: physics("mf").create("vlt1", "Velocity", 2); set("v", new String[]{"0", "0", "v0"})

parameters.name: v
parameters.description: Velocity field (m/s), optionally in a rotated/cylindrical coordinate system (e.g. Omega*sys2.r in the azimuthal direction).

parameters.name: coordinateSystem
parameters.description: Coordinate system for the velocity components.

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Devices,_Transducers_and_Actuators/falling_magnet, magnetic_brake and ACDC_Module/Devices,_Motors_and_Generators/homopolar_generator.
tools.notes: If the moving body is bounded in the direction of motion or carries magnets, use a moving mesh/Rotating Domain instead.

tools.name: Tangential Magnetic Vector Potential (Magnetic Fields)
tools.description: Boundary condition n x A = n x A0 that prescribes the tangential magnetic vector potential (the normal component is free). Use it to impose a known external field distribution or flux on a boundary; with the Reduced field background formulation it behaves like Magnetic Insulation for the reduced field.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields / Magnetic and Electric Fields > Boundaries > Tangential Magnetic Vector Potential. Java: physics("mef").create("mp1", "MagneticPotential", 2); set("A0", new String[]{...})

parameters.name: A0
parameters.description: Magnetic vector potential (Wb/m) on the boundary.

parameters.name: Constraint settings
parameters.description: Advanced Physics Options (pointwise/weak).

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Motors_and_Generators/homopolar_generator (Magnetic and Electric Fields) uses a Tangential Magnetic Vector Potential boundary condition together with Velocity (Lorentz Term) on the rotating disc.
tools.notes: Background Magnetic Flux Density (mef) sets A0 from a uniform B_b automatically but is incompatible with Periodic Condition.

tools.name: Tangential Magnetic Field (Magnetic Fields / Magnetic Field Formulation)
tools.description: Boundary condition n x H = n x H0 that prescribes the tangential magnetic field on exterior boundaries; it is the natural way to apply an external field (plane-wave-like excitation in magnetotellurics, an applied field around a superconductor) or a symmetric field condition. In Magnetic Field Formulation the corresponding node is called Magnetic Field and supports exclusive Harmonic Perturbation.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields > Boundaries > Tangential Magnetic Field; Magnetic Field Formulation > Magnetic Field. Java: physics("mf").create("mfb1", "MagneticFieldBoundary", 2); set("H0", new String[]{...})

parameters.name: H0
parameters.description: Magnetic field (A/m); only the tangential part is enforced.

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Devices,_Resistive/magnetotellurics (mf) and ACDC_Module/Devices,_Superconducting/superconducting_wire (mfh, applied field ramp).
tools.notes: Magnetic Insulation (n x A = 0) is the default alternative; Perfect Magnetic Conductor forces n x H = 0.

tools.name: Surface Current Density (Magnetic Fields)
tools.description: Boundary source that applies a surface current density Js0 (A/m) on exterior boundaries (-n x H = Js) or interior boundaries (jump in tangential H), representing thin current sheets such as foil windings, PCB traces or eddy-current sheets computed elsewhere. Supports Harmonic Perturbation; also available in Magnetic and Electric Fields.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields > Boundaries > Surface Current Density. Java: physics("mf").create("scu1", "SurfaceCurrent", 2); set("Js0", new String[]{...})

parameters.name: Js0
parameters.description: Surface current density vector (A/m), default 0.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Inductive/planar_pcb_coil: surface current from an Electric Currents in Shells solution drives the magnetic field of the PCB spiral.
tools.notes: A Surface Current Density subnode also exists under Transition Boundary Condition for impressed currents on thin sheets.

tools.name: Surface Magnetic Current Density (Magnetic Fields)
tools.description: Boundary condition that imposes a fictitious surface magnetic current density Jms0 (V/m) on exterior or interior boundaries, i.e. a jump in the tangential electric field. The vector is projected onto the surface (normal component ignored). It is used for equivalent-source formulations and to impress a tangential E discontinuity; Magnetic Field Formulation has the same node.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields / Magnetic Field Formulation > Boundaries > Surface Magnetic Current Density

parameters.name: Jms0
parameters.description: Surface magnetic current density (V/m).

tools.example: Impress a voltage gap around a cut in a conducting ring in mfh: Surface Magnetic Current Density with Jms0 = V0/d along the ring direction on the cut boundary.
tools.notes: Java type string not present in the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: Periodic Magnetic Continuity (Magnetic Fields pair)
tools.description: Pair condition (Pairs menu) that applies a periodic (continuity or antiperiodic) condition on the magnetic vector potential across identity/contact pairs, used to connect a moving part and a stator in linear machines where only a finite periodic section is modelled. It differs from Periodic Condition, which acts on ordinary boundaries rather than pairs.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields > Pairs > Periodic Magnetic Continuity. Java: physics("mf").create("pp1", "PeriodicPair", 1); set("pairs", ...)

parameters.name: Pair selection
parameters.description: From list (default), All, All contact pairs or All identity pairs.

parameters.name: Constraint settings
parameters.description: Advanced Physics Options.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Motors_and_Generators/linear_motor_2d: translator and stator periodic boundaries linked with Periodic Magnetic Continuity while the translator moves with a moving mesh.
tools.notes: Rotating machines use Continuity/Sector Symmetry pairs (rmm) or Rotational Magnetic Continuity (mmtp).

tools.name: Exterior Electric Insulation (Magnetic Fields)
tools.description: Exterior boundary condition of Magnetic Fields that enforces electric insulation (no normal current) by applying a truncated magnetic scalar potential condition. It must be applied to exterior boundaries of conducting domains and of the surrounding nonconducting domains, and it helps satisfy the topological rules of the mixed A–Vm formulation in 3D Rotating Machinery, Magnetic models.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields > Boundaries > Exterior Electric Insulation

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Exterior boundaries only.

tools.example: 3D motor sector cut at the axial mid-plane: apply Exterior Electric Insulation on the cut face of the rotor bars and the adjacent air so no current leaves through the symmetry plane.
tools.notes: Java type string not present in the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: External Magnetic Vector Potential (reduced-field Magnetic Fields)
tools.description: Boundary condition available when the Magnetic Fields interface solves for the Reduced field with a background magnetic vector potential: it forces the reduced potential to zero, i.e. the total field equals the background field, on exterior boundaries far enough away that the object does not disturb the background. Use it with a uniform or analytic background field (e.g. MHD duct flow in an applied field, objects in the Earth's field).
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields > Settings > Background Field: Solve for Reduced field; Boundaries > External Magnetic Vector Potential. Java: physics("mf").create("exvp1", "ExternalMagneticVectorPotential", 2)

parameters.name: Background magnetic vector potential A_b
parameters.description: Set on the interface Background Field section.

parameters.name: Constraint settings
parameters.description: Pointwise/weak constraints.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Electromagnetics_and_Fluids/hartmann_boundary_layer: uniform applied field as background A_b, External Magnetic Vector Potential on the channel boundaries.
tools.notes: Magnetic Fields, No Currents counterpart: External Magnetic Flux Density.

tools.name: Layered Transition / Layered Impedance Boundary Condition (Magnetic Fields)
tools.description: Frequency-domain boundary conditions that model stacks of thin metallic layers defined by a Layered Material: Layered Transition Boundary Condition (interior) relates the tangential-E discontinuity to the surface currents on each layer using per-layer transfer and surface impedances, and Layered Impedance Boundary Condition (exterior) combines such a layer stack with an Impedance Boundary Condition for the substrate underneath, assuming mainly normal propagation into the layers.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields > Boundaries > Layered Transition Boundary Condition / Layered Impedance Boundary Condition (Frequency Domain); requires a Layered Material or Layered Material Link

parameters.name: Shell properties / layered material
parameters.description: Layer thicknesses and materials (conductivity, permeability, permittivity).

parameters.name: Layer and interface selection
parameters.description: Which layers of the stack are included.

tools.example: Plated shielding can (Cu + Ni on steel): Layered Impedance Boundary Condition on the can surface with a 3-layer Layered Material, Frequency Domain 10 kHz-10 MHz.
tools.notes: Single-layer versions are the Transition Boundary Condition and Impedance Boundary Condition (mf), catalogued separately.

tools.name: Thin Low Permeability Gap (Magnetic Fields / No Currents)
tools.description: Interior- and pair-boundary condition that represents a thin gap (thickness ds, relative permeability mu_r lower than the surroundings) in a magnetic circuit, such as an air gap or nonmagnetic spacer in a core, without meshing it. In Magnetic and Electric Fields it can carry Electric Insulation, Contact Impedance and Electrical Contact subnodes for the electrical side.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields / Magnetic Fields, No Currents > Boundaries > Thin Low Permeability Gap

parameters.name: mu_r
parameters.description: Relative permeability of the gap (From material or user defined, isotropic to full).

parameters.name: ds
parameters.description: Surface thickness of the gap (default 1 m; always set it).

tools.example: Gapped ferrite E-core inductor: Thin Low Permeability Gap with ds = 0.2 mm, mu_r = 1 on the center-leg interface instead of a sliver domain.
tools.notes: High-permeability thin sheets use Magnetic Shielding instead. Java type string not present in the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: Magnetic Point Dipole (Magnetic Fields)
tools.description: Point source in 2D and 3D representing an infinitesimal current loop of dipole moment m (m^2·A), the limit of a loop whose area goes to zero while I*a stays finite; the direction follows the right-hand rule of the current. Specify Magnitude and direction or the full Dipole moment vector. The 2D-axisymmetric variant is Magnetic Point Dipole (on Axis).
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields > Points > Magnetic Point Dipole

parameters.name: Dipole specification
parameters.description: Magnitude and direction or Dipole moment.

parameters.name: n_m, m
parameters.description: Direction and magnitude of the magnetic dipole moment.

tools.example: Eddy-current NDT probe approximated as a point dipole m = 1e-3 A·m^2 above a plate with an Impedance Boundary Condition, Frequency Domain 100 kHz.
tools.notes: Java type string not present in the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: Magnetic Scalar Potential / Zero Magnetic Scalar Potential / Normal Magnetic Flux Density (mfnc boundary conditions)
tools.description: Scalar-potential boundary conditions of Magnetic Fields, No Currents (and its BEM version): Magnetic Scalar Potential fixes Vm = Vm0 (A), Zero Magnetic Scalar Potential sets Vm = 0 (a flux-normal 'magnetic ground', often on symmetry planes of antisymmetric fields), and Normal Magnetic Flux Density prescribes either an Inward flux density Bn or a full B0 vector whose normal component is used. Differences of Vm across two boundaries drive a magnetomotive force through the region.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields, No Currents > Boundaries > Magnetic Scalar Potential / Zero Magnetic Scalar Potential / Normal Magnetic Flux Density. Java: physics("mfnc").create("zsp1", "ZeroMagneticScalarPotential", 2); mfncbe normal flux type MagneticFluxDensity

parameters.name: Vm0
parameters.description: Magnetic scalar potential value (default 0 A).

parameters.name: Type (Normal Magnetic Flux Density)
parameters.description: Inward flux density Bn (positive inward) or Magnetic flux density B0.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Capacitive/hall_effect_sensor uses Zero Magnetic Scalar Potential in its mfnc model; force_calculation_03_magnetic_torque_bem uses Normal Magnetic Flux Density in mfncbe.
tools.notes: Magnetic Insulation (n·B = 0) is the default mfnc condition.

tools.name: External Magnetic Flux Density (reduced-field Magnetic Fields, No Currents)
tools.description: Boundary condition available when Magnetic Fields, No Currents solves for the Reduced field with a background magnetic flux density: it forces the reduced flux density to zero on exterior boundaries so the total field equals the background there. Use it for magnetized objects in a uniform applied field such as a ship hull in the Earth's field or ore bodies in geomagnetic surveys.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields, No Currents > Settings > Background Field: Reduced field; Boundaries > External Magnetic Flux Density. Java: physics("mfnc").create("exfd1", "ExternalMagneticFluxDensity", 2)

parameters.name: Background magnetic flux density B_b
parameters.description: Defined in the interface Background Field section.

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Introductory_Magnetostatics/magnetic_prospecting and magnetic_signature_submarine (background geomagnetic field, submarine hull as Magnetic Shielding).
tools.notes: Place the boundaries far from the object or use infinite elements.

tools.name: Magnetic Scalar Potential Discontinuity (Magnetic Fields, No Currents)
tools.description: Interior-boundary condition that prescribes a jump Vm_up - Vm_down across a cut. Applied on a cut that makes a multiply connected region simply connected, it formally represents a surface current circulating around the cut's edges, so current loops (coils) can be emulated in the scalar-potential interface without solving for A.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields, No Currents > Boundaries > Magnetic Scalar Potential Discontinuity

parameters.name: Delta Vm
parameters.description: Potential difference across the boundary (A), equal to the enclosed ampere-turns.

tools.example: Model a racetrack coil's field in mfnc: add a cut surface spanning the coil opening and set Delta Vm = N*I.
tools.notes: Java type string not present in the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: Boundary Force Calculation (Magnetic Fields, No Currents)
tools.description: Boundary-level force and torque evaluation for Magnetic Fields, No Currents based on the Virtual Gap Method: the Maxwell stress is expressed with only the continuous components (tangential H and normal B) to avoid contamination from discontinuous field components. It defines <tag>.Force<comp>_<name>, <tag>.Torque<comp>_<name> and axial torque <tag>.Tax_<name> with a torque axis and rotation point; Split by Connectivity creates one node per connected body.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields, No Currents > Boundaries > Boundary Force Calculation. Java: physics("mfnc").create("bfcal1", "BoundaryForceCalculation", 2); set("ForceName", "plate")

parameters.name: ForceName
parameters.description: Suffix for the force/torque variables.

parameters.name: TorqueAxis, TorqueRotationPoint
parameters.description: Axis r_ax and point r0 for torque.

parameters.name: ForceCalculationMethod / useAverage
parameters.description: Automatic method and averaging of the two sides.

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Introductory_Magnetostatics/one_sided_magnet and permanent_magnet: attraction force mfnc.Forcez_plate on an iron plate.
tools.notes: Domain-level Force Calculation (Maxwell stress on the domain's exterior) is catalogued as 'Force Calculation'. In 2D axisymmetry the radial force is zero by symmetry.

tools.name: Magnetic Scalar–Scalar / Vector–Scalar Potential Coupling (BEM couplings)
tools.description: Multiphysics couplings that join a finite-element magnetic interface to the Magnetic Fields, No Currents, Boundary Elements interface on shared boundaries: Magnetic Scalar–Scalar Potential Coupling makes the scalar potential continuous between Magnetic Fields, Currents Only (or mfnc FEM) and mfncbe, and Magnetic Vector–Scalar Potential Coupling ensures continuity of B between Magnetic Fields (A) and mfncbe. The BEM part then represents the unbounded air.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Magnetic Scalar–Scalar Potential Coupling (type MagneticScalarScalarPotentialCoupling) / Magnetic Vector–Scalar Potential Coupling

parameters.name: Boundary selection
parameters.description: FEM/BEM interface boundaries (Manual or All boundaries).

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Primary FEM interface and the mfncbe interface.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Introductory_Electromagnetic_Forces/force_calculation_02_magnetic_force_bem: iron parts in mfnc FEM coupled to mfncbe air with Magnetic Scalar–Scalar Potential Coupling.
tools.notes: With Magnetic Fields, use Gauge Fixing for A-Field and a Fully Coupled direct solver; for reduced-field mf add a Tangential Magnetic Field with the background field on the coupling boundary.

tools.name: Faraday's Law (Magnetic Field Formulation)
tools.description: Main domain node of the Magnetic Field Formulation interface that adds Faraday's law for H with B-H relations (relative permeability, B-H curve, magnetic losses, etc.) and a Jc-E relation expressed as resistivity: Electrical resistivity or an E-J characteristic (E as a function of |J|) such as the power law E = E0*(|J|/Jc)^n used for superconductors. Relative permittivity can add displacement currents.
tools.usage: Magnetic Field Formulation > Faraday's Law (default). Java: physics("mfh").feature("fl1"); set("ConstitutiveRelationJcE", "EJCharacteristic"); set("normE", "E0*(mfh.normJ/Jc)^n")

parameters.name: ConstitutiveRelationJcE
parameters.description: ElectricalResistivity (rho, or linearized rho0/alpha/Tref) or EJCharacteristic (normE as function of mfh.normJ).

parameters.name: ConstitutiveRelationBH
parameters.description: RelativePermeability or nonlinear B-H options.

parameters.name: Loss Calculation subnode
parameters.description: Available for AC loss evaluation.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Superconducting/superconducting_wire: EJCharacteristic (E as a function of mfh.normJ) with critical current density and n-value for the superconducting tape.
tools.notes: The formulation needs finite resistivity everywhere; the Tangential Electric Field boundary node applies source electric fields on conductor boundaries.

tools.name: Magnetic Gauss' Law (Magnetic Field Formulation)
tools.description: Default node of Magnetic Field Formulation (3D and 2D in-plane) that enforces div B = 0 through an auxiliary potential-like variable psi whose absolute value is irrelevant (only its gradient enters). The Divergence condition variable scaling Psi0 (default 1 A) sets its magnitude, and advanced options constrain psi in at least one point and choose Constrain value or Constrain tangential gradient on boundaries.
tools.usage: Magnetic Field Formulation > Magnetic Gauss' Law. Java: physics("mfh").feature("mgl1") (type MagneticGaussLaw)

parameters.name: Psi0
parameters.description: Divergence condition variable scaling (default 1 A).

parameters.name: Constrain variable in at least one point
parameters.description: Removes the null space of psi.

parameters.name: Method
parameters.description: Constrain value (default) or Constrain tangential gradient.

tools.example: Keep the default Magnetic Gauss' Law in a 3D HTS coil model; disable it only for 2D out-of-plane field models where it is not needed.
tools.notes: Analogous in purpose to Gauge Fixing for A-Field in the A-formulation.

tools.name: Magnetic Fields Formulation–No Currents Coupling (mfh–mfnc)
tools.description: Multiphysics coupling that ensures continuity of normal B and tangential H between a Magnetic Field Formulation region (conductors, superconductors) and a Magnetic Fields, No Currents region (surrounding air), so the air needs no artificial conductivity and only a scalar potential. Primary interface is mfnc, secondary is mfh.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Magnetic Fields Formulation Magnetic Fields No Currents Coupling (when both mfh and mfnc exist)

parameters.name: Boundary selection
parameters.description: Manual or All boundaries (exterior mfnc boundaries touching mfh boundaries).

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Primary: Magnetic Fields, No Currents; Secondary: Magnetic Field Formulation.

tools.example: HTS cable: mfh on the tapes (E-J power law), mfnc on the air, coupling on the tape surfaces; much smaller and better-conditioned system than all-mfh.
tools.notes: The air region must be simply connected for a scalar potential or contain cuts.

tools.name: Conductor / Multiterminal Conductor (Magnetic Fields, Currents Only)
tools.description: Domain nodes of Magnetic Fields, Currents Only that solve current continuity in conductors with a given conductivity and subnodes Terminal, Ground and Electric Insulation, providing the current source for the Biot–Savart-like field and the inductance matrix. Conductor handles one terminal per conductor; Multiterminal Conductor handles conductors with several current inputs. 'Split by Connectivity' generates one node (or Terminal) per geometrically connected part; use with Stationary Source Sweep with Initialization.
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields, Currents Only > Conductor / Multiterminal Conductor > Terminal, Ground. Java: physics("mfco").create("cond1", "Conductor", 3); feature("cond1").create("term1", "Terminal", 2)

parameters.name: sigma
parameters.description: Conductor conductivity (e.g. 6e7 S/m).

parameters.name: TerminalName
parameters.description: Index used for the inductance matrix mfco.L.

parameters.name: Split by Connectivity
parameters.description: Right-click operation to create separate nodes/terminals.

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Devices,_Inductive/helmholtz_coil and inductance_matrix_pcb_coils (Source Initialization + Stationary/Frequency Domain Source Sweep).
tools.notes: External Current Density can replace Conductor when the current distribution is known or imported from Electric Currents.

tools.name: Ampère's Law and Current Conservation (Magnetic and Electric Fields)
tools.description: Main domain node of Magnetic and Electric Fields (mef) solving Ampère's law and the current continuity equation together in the A-V formulation, with B-H, Jc-E and D-E constitutive relations. In 6.4 it comes in Solids and Fluids variants (material vs spatial frame; replacing the Material type switch of 6.2 and earlier) and can be overridden locally by Ampère's Law (A only) or Coil features.
tools.usage: Magnetic and Electric Fields > Ampère's Law and Current Conservation in Solids / in Fluids. Java: physics("mef").create("alcs1", "ElectromagneticModelSolid", 3); fluids: "ElectromagneticModelFluid"

parameters.name: ConstitutiveRelationBH
parameters.description: Relative permeability, remanent flux density, magnetic losses, B-H curve, etc.

parameters.name: ConstitutiveRelationJcE
parameters.description: Conductivity, linearized resistivity, Hall effect...

parameters.name: ConstitutiveRelationDE
parameters.description: Relative permittivity and dielectric loss options.

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Devices,_Inductive/power_inductor and ACDC_Module/Devices,_Transducers_and_Actuators/magnetic_brake (conducting disc with Velocity (Lorentz Term)).
tools.notes: The MHD and Arc Discharge multiphysics interfaces use the Fluids variant in the conducting fluid/plasma.

tools.name: RLC Coil Group (Magnetic and Electric Fields)
tools.description: 2D/2D-axisymmetric coil feature of Magnetic and Electric Fields that combines the magnetic model of a single-turn coil group with a multiterminal electrical model for in-plane current, so capacitive leakage between turns (self-resonance, turn-to-turn capacitance) is captured in 2D. Each turn cross-section is held at a constant potential (V removed by an Ampère's Law node) and a balance between out-of-plane and in-plane leakage currents is enforced; valid when in-plane current is small compared with the coil current.
tools.usage: Magnetic and Electric Fields > RLC Coil Group (on domains with Ampère's Law active). Java: physics("mef").create("rlccg1", "RLCCoilGroup", 2); set("CoilExcitation", "Voltage"); set("VCoil", "1[V]")

parameters.name: CoilExcitation
parameters.description: Current or Voltage (circuit options available).

parameters.name: DomainSpec / DomainsList / Ordering / Winding
parameters.description: Turn order: manual list or automatic row-wise ordering, regular winding.

parameters.name: ICoil / VCoil / PCoil
parameters.description: Excitation value.

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Tutorials,_Coils/resonant_spiral_coil_2daxi and ACDC_Module/Devices,_Inductive/axisymmetric_approximation_of_inductor_3d (frequency sweep through self-resonance).
tools.notes: For strong in-plane currents use a full 3D model instead.

tools.name: Background Magnetic Flux Density (Magnetic and Electric Fields)
tools.description: Boundary condition of Magnetic and Electric Fields that imposes n x A = n x A_b where A_b is constructed so that curl A_b = B_b for a user-given uniform background flux density B_b. It is the simplest way to apply an external field in MHD and arc models; it is incompatible with Periodic Condition (then use Tangential Magnetic Vector Potential with consistent values).
tools.usage: Magnetic and Electric Fields > Boundaries > Background Magnetic Flux Density. Java: physics("mef").create("bmfd1", "BackgroundMagneticFluxDensity", 2); set("Bb", new String[]{"0", "0", "B0"})

parameters.name: Bb
parameters.description: Background magnetic flux density vector (T).

parameters.name: Constraint settings
parameters.description: Advanced Physics Options.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Electromagnetics_and_Fluids/hartmann_flow_in_liquid_metal_blanket: B0 applied transversely to a liquid-metal duct.
tools.notes: Only the tangential components are guaranteed to match.
